title: Excavations against the North Wall of Jerusalem, 1937-8
author: R. W. Hamilton
location_note: Soundings A-E at the Damascus Gate and along the north wall of the Old City, Jerusalem; no map reference; placed by name.
reading: pp. 1-4 in full; then eligible-class keyword paragraphs, with the cistern (pp. 21-26) and aqueduct (pp. 38-41, 50-53) sections read in full
notes: Soundings against the Damascus Gate towers and the north wall 1937-8: wall phases from Aelia Capitolina (or later) to the 6th-7th c. and Islamic work; pottery and coin tables. A circular rubble-lined cesspit against the tower is not an eligible class (not coded). Drain-pipe fragments are finds, not features. The Fatalis tombstone is re-used in the aqueduct inspection chamber (not a burial feature).

features.site: Damascus Gate, east and west of the gate (soundings D and E)
features.subtype: two vaulted, plastered cisterns in the angles between towers and curtain; west cistern possibly by the builders of the tower revetment
features.period: not dated (incorporate older masonry; manhole heightened in Turkish times)
features.quote: the two cisterns which occupy the angles between the towers

features.site: sounding C, under the city wall
features.subtype: rock-cut, plastered and slab-covered aqueduct with inspection chamber and manholes
features.period: earlier than soil B (contents not later than 1st-2nd c. AD); in use and repaired until the 3rd or early 4th c. AD
features.quote: This is an aqueduct, which was found running from north to south

features.site: sounding A, north face of the west tower
features.quote: the presence of a modern flood drain which passes close

features.subtype: quarried rock scarp (fosse) cutting the aqueduct, part of the great quarry of Solomon's Caverns
features.period: fosse dug after the third or early fourth century AD
features.quote: the fosse was not dug till after the third or early fourth
